reconciliationSummary: Two codex reviewers (epic-reviewer-1, epic-reviewer-2) blocked; two Claude reviewers (epic-reviewer-3, epic-reviewer-4) passed. Independent verification of the three contested findings resolves all downward. (1) EPIC7-B001 — no first-party producers for five of seven archive kinds: confirmed in code (script-execution.service.ts emits archiveEntries: []). However, Epic 7 scope covers the archive infrastructure, not a model-driven runtime. The team-impl-log records this as accepted platform-standup state and the source comment states the payload 'must not synthesize canonical archive entries'. Tests exercise all seven entry kinds via fixtures against the Convex primitive. This is a scope-conformant observation, not a blocking violation. Downgraded to CANON-N001. (2) EPIC7-B002 — stale cache during deferred reconciliation: confirmed that computeArchiveSignature fingerprints only archiveEntryId:sequence:recordedAt, omitting provenance and status fields. However, patchArchiveEntry already calls invalidateArchiveDerivedCaches atomically (convex/archiveEntries.ts:226), deleting all cached turns and views before returning. The residual risk is a narrow race where a concurrent rebuild reads pre-patch state and repopulates the cache after the invalidation; effect is transient inconsistency, not data corruption or data loss. Downgraded to CANON-N002. (3) epic7-public-convex-archive-bypass — public Convex archive functions lack apiKey gating: confirmed that archiveEntries and archiveTurns export raw mutation/query without the *ForService+apiKey pattern that derivedArchiveViews uses. However, a codebase grep found no ConvexProvider, ConvexReactClient, or VITE_CONVEX URL in the client directory; Convex is accessed exclusively server-side through ConvexPlatformStore. The public mutations validate processId/projectId ownership. The pattern is consistent with other repo tables (processes.ts, processOutputs.ts, sourceProvenance.ts). This is an asymmetric hardening gap from Story 5, not an end-user-accessible security bypass. Downgraded to CANON-N003. Both verification gates (green-verify and verify-all) passed in two independent codex runs, and all eight story gates passed in the team-impl-log. The epic infrastructure is correctly implemented with the platform-standup-state limitations explicitly documented and accepted.
crossStoryFindings: All eight stories compose correctly into the intended archive → turns → structural views flow: canonical entry persistence (Story 1) → finalization boundary (Story 2) → read/reopen surface (Story 3) → turn derivation (Story 4) → structural views (Story 5) → provenance enrichment (Story 6) → degraded-state hardening (Story 7). No cross-story schema or ID drift found.

Cache invalidation is consistent end-to-end: appendArchiveEntry and patchArchiveEntry in convex/archiveEntries.ts delete all cached archiveTurns and derivedArchiveViews atomically; upsertArchiveTurns in convex/archiveTurns.ts deletes all cached derivedArchiveViews. This preserves the tech-design contract that turns and views are rebuildable projections, never canonical truth.

Deferred archive patching (applyExecutionResultSideEffects writes a degraded row first, reconcileDeferredArchiveEntries patches later) correctly invalidates cached turns and views on patch. The computeArchiveSignature fingerprint in derived-archive-view.service.ts omits provenance and status fields, leaving a narrow race where a concurrent rebuild can repopulate the cache from pre-patch archive state after the patch invalidation. Effect is transient inconsistency, not permanent data corruption.

Turn IDs are stable deterministic strings (processId:turn:turnIndex); derived view IDs are deterministic (processId:derived-view:viewKind:startIndex-endIndex). Provenance remains traceable across cache rebuilds as the tech design requires.

The first-party runtime archives only user_message (via process-response.service.ts) and process_event (bridged via appendFromProcessHistoryItem). The remaining five PRD-mandated entry kinds (model_message, reasoning, script_emission, tool_call, tool_result) are accepted by the Convex primitive and exercised by tests, but the default integrated execution payload returns archiveEntries: []. This is accepted platform-standup state per the team-impl-log and does not violate Epic 7 scope, which covers archive infrastructure rather than model-driven runtime content.
architectureFindings: Module layout matches the tech design: convex/archiveEntries.ts, convex/archiveTurns.ts, convex/derivedArchiveViews.ts, convex/schema.ts, archive services, archive routes, contracts, and client sections are all present and wired as specified.

Fastify owns finalization policy and access enforcement; Convex owns atomic sequence assignment, idempotency guard, and durable storage — consistent with the architecture split. Route handlers call processAccessService.assertProcessAccess before any archive read service runs.

Asymmetric apiKey gating: convex/derivedArchiveViews.ts uses internalMutation/internalQuery plus *ForService apiKey-checked public wrappers (Story 5 hardening). convex/archiveEntries.ts and convex/archiveTurns.ts expose raw mutation/query. Browser clients have no direct Convex access (no ConvexProvider or VITE_CONVEX URL in client code), so the practical security risk is low. The pattern inconsistency relative to Story 5 is a cohesion gap worth resolving in a follow-up.

computeArchiveSignature in derived-archive-view.service.ts fingerprints only archiveEntryId:sequence:recordedAt. Patches to relatedArtifactVersionId, relatedSourceProvenanceId, relatedToolCallId, entryStatus, or degradationReason via patchArchiveEntry are invisible to the conflict detector. Since patchArchiveEntry also invalidates the cache atomically, the residual risk is a narrow concurrent-rebuild race rather than a systematic data integrity gap.

NullPlatformStore is correctly rejected in production (createApp enforces this at startup). It boots without error in non-production, returning synthetic archive responses — a deliberate fallback documented in source comments.
epicCoverageAssessment: AC-1.x (canonical entry persistence, taxonomy, ordering, idempotency, related-id links): Covered. convex/archiveEntries.ts appendArchiveEntry validates all seven entry kinds via a Set, assigns sequence atomically, and enforces finalizationKey idempotency per process.

AC-2.x (live/archive separation, finalization boundary): Covered. ArchiveFinalizationService is called only from completion points — accepted user responses (process-response.service.ts) and completed runtime objects (process-environment.service.ts). Raw deltas and interrupted partials never call append.

AC-3.x (archive read, reopen, access boundaries, degraded entry display): Covered. processAccessService.assertProcessAccess is called before every archive read. Empty and degraded states flow through the archivePageSchema parse contract.

AC-4.x (turn derivation, archive-entry immutability, degraded turn handling): Covered. deriveTurnsFromArchiveEntries is deterministic over sorted entries. Degradation propagates from entries to turns without mutating archive rows.

AC-5.x (structural derived views without model-generated summaries): Covered. buildDerivedArchiveViews generates turn_range and chunk_candidate views with deterministic structural labels only; no model-generated content path exists.

AC-6.x (artifact and source provenance enrichment, per-entry degradation): Covered. enrichArchiveEntries batches artifact version and source provenance lookups; each entry degrades independently when its related record is unavailable.

AC-7.x (reload/environment-loss survival, bounded reads, derived-view failure isolation): Covered. All reads use durable Convex storage. Pagination limits are enforced. Archive reads succeed when derived-view refresh throws — routes handle them independently.

Service tests for non-user archive kinds inject RuntimeArchiveEntry fixtures directly; no checked-in production execution path emits model_message, reasoning, script_emission, tool_call, or tool_result. Tests prove the infrastructure works; the production producer gap is accepted scope-defer per team-impl-log.

Browser e2e test (archive-runtime-flow.spec.ts) uses InMemoryPlatformStore with pre-populated fixtures and validates routing, shell, and UI rendering against a live Fastify server. It does not exercise a ConvexPlatformStore durable-storage round-trip. Acceptable for Epic 7 closeout; convex/archiveEntries.test.ts and service suites cover durable behavior.
productionPathFindings: ConvexPlatformStore is the production store and calls real Convex functions: appendArchiveEntry, upsertArchiveTurns, replaceDerivedArchiveViewsForService, and corresponding reads. No shims or fake adapters on the production path.
DefaultArchiveReadService, DefaultTurnDerivationService, and DefaultDerivedArchiveViewService are instantiated unconditionally in app.ts when not overridden via test options.

NullPlatformStore and InMemoryPlatformStore are test doubles only. NullPlatformStore is explicitly rejected in production (createApp throws when NODE_ENV=production or LIMINAL_VITE_RUNTIME_MODE=production). InMemoryPlatformStore is only reachable via test options.

The default integrated execution payload (buildIntegratedWorkspaceExecutionSource) sets archiveEntries: [] and emits a single process_event history item per run. Canonical archive rows for model_message, reasoning, script_emission, tool_call, and tool_result are not produced by any checked-in production code path. Explicitly accepted as platform-standup state in the team-impl-log and in source-level comments.

archiveFinalizationService is constructed with a default new ArchiveFinalizationService(platformStore) inside ProcessEnvironmentService and ProcessResponseService constructors. In production, platformStore resolves to ConvexPlatformStore, so the archive finalization path is real and durable.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Production runtime emits only two of the seven canonical archive entry kinds
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts buildIntegratedWorkspaceExecutionSource returns archiveEntries: [] in its result payload. process-environment.service.ts bridges process_event from history items; process-response.service.ts archives user_message on accepted responses. No checked-in production code path emits model_message, reasoning, script_emission, tool_call, or tool_result. The Convex primitive and service layer accept all seven kinds and tests exercise them via fixtures. The team-impl-log records this as accepted platform-standup state; the source comment explicitly notes the payload 'must not synthesize canonical archive entries'. Epic 7 scope covers archive infrastructure, not model-driven runtime content.

nonBlockingFindings.title: computeArchiveSignature omits provenance and status fields; concurrent rebuild can repopulate cache from pre-patch archive state
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts:262-270 fingerprints only archiveEntryId:sequence:recordedAt. Patches to relatedArtifactVersionId, relatedSourceProvenanceId, relatedToolCallId, entryStatus, or degradationReason via convex/archiveEntries.ts patchArchiveEntry are invisible to the drift detector. patchArchiveEntry calls invalidateArchiveDerivedCaches atomically (convex/archiveEntries.ts:226) deleting cached turns and views. The residual risk is a narrow race: a turn rebuild that started before the patch lands and completes after the cache was cleared will upsert turns derived from pre-patch archive state, repopulating the cache with stale projections. A subsequent derived-view refresh would then read those stale turns. Effect is transient inconsistency rather than permanent data corruption.

nonBlockingFindings.title: archiveEntries and archiveTurns Convex functions lack the apiKey gate that derivedArchiveViews uses
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: convex/archiveEntries.ts:94, :150, :182 and convex/archiveTurns.ts:45, :96 expose appendArchiveEntry, listArchiveEntries, patchArchiveEntry, upsertArchiveTurns, and listArchiveTurns as raw mutation/query without the apiKey check that convex/derivedArchiveViews.ts:91-107 adds via replaceDerivedArchiveViewsForService. A grep of the client directory found no ConvexProvider, ConvexReactClient, or VITE_CONVEX URL exposure; Convex is accessed exclusively server-side by ConvexPlatformStore. The mutations validate processId/projectId ownership. The pattern is consistent with repo convention for other tables (processes.ts, processOutputs.ts, sourceProvenance.ts) but asymmetric with the Story 5 hardening pattern applied to derivedArchiveViews.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Derived-view Convex pagination reads the prefix on every page (O(p²) over page index)
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: convex/derivedArchiveViews.ts listDerivedArchiveViews decodes a numeric offset cursor and calls .take(args.limit + decodedCursor + 1), then slices. Page N loads N×limit rows server-side. Total derived views per process are structurally bounded (~1.5× turn count) and the route caps limit at 50, so behavior stays bounded for realistic process sizes but has a quadratic scaling shape if process sizes grow. apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts also accepts any digit-only cursor without range validation.

nonBlockingFindings.title: appendFinalizedEntry enforces non-null sourceObjectId for all entry kinds; spec marks it optional
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-finalization.service.ts:31-33 throws for any null sourceObjectId regardless of entry kind. The epic schema marks sourceObjectId optional (nullable when not applicable). If a runtime emits a reasoning or script_emission entry without a sourceObjectId, appendFinalizedEntry will throw rather than delegating to the Convex layer's nullable schema.

nonBlockingFindings.title: NullPlatformStore boots without error outside production, masking missing Convex configuration in local/staging environments
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: apps/platform/server/app.ts:190-227 defaults to NullPlatformStore when hasLiveConvexConfig returns false, only hard-failing when NODE_ENV=production or LIMINAL_VITE_RUNTIME_MODE=production. NullPlatformStore returns synthetic archive write acknowledgements and empty archive/turn/derived-view reads. This is a deliberate non-real path but can mask missing Convex configuration in non-production environments.

nonBlockingFindings.title: listAllArchiveEntries pagination helper is duplicated across two service files
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: An identical pagination loop appears in both apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts (lines 159-182) and apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts (lines 273-296). Implementations are semantically identical. Not a functional problem but a cohesion gap relative to the module responsibility matrix.

nonBlockingFindings.title: hasStoredTurns check in getTurns is redundant after storedPage.turns.length === 0 is confirmed
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts:103 calls hasStoredTurns (limit:1) after storedPage.turns.length === 0 has already been established. Both queries hit the same first page with cursor=null; the extra round-trip cannot return a different result.

nonBlockingFindings.title: void archiveRoutePatterns statement in archive.ts is a code smell
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: apps/platform/server/routes/archive.ts:59 contains `void archiveRoutePatterns;` which evaluates and discards an object. Appears to suppress a lint warning about an unused import rather than serving any runtime purpose.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Derived view page limit of 50 may truncate views for processes with 25+ turns
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts MAX_DERIVED_ARCHIVE_VIEW_LIMIT=50. buildDerivedArchiveViews emits one turn_range per turn plus one chunk_candidate per two turns, so a process with 34+ turns generates more than 50 views. Pagination is plumbed but client sections may not surface the next-page cursor to users yet.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Default integrated execution payload is a static template rather than a model-driven runtime
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:20-296 builds execution source using a runtimeProfileByProcessType lookup that hard-codes artifact title, source note title, history text, and commit message per process type. Real files are written and real checkpoint candidates produced, but synthesis content is not model-generated. Source comment documents this as intentional: 'The default payload may produce runtime artifacts/checkpoint candidates, but it must not synthesize canonical archive entries.'

nonBlockingFindings.title: Archive e2e test validates routing and UI against InMemoryPlatformStore, not a real Convex durable-storage round-trip
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: tests/e2e/archive-runtime-flow.spec.ts:67-86 constructs InMemoryPlatformStore with pre-populated archive/turn/view fixtures and passes it via buildApp's platformStore option. Playwright asserts on rendered DOM against a live Fastify server. This validates routing, shell, and UI rendering but does not exercise ConvexPlatformStore. Acceptable for Epic 7 closeout; convex/archiveEntries.test.ts and service suites cover durable behavior.

unresolvedItems: Whether the apiKey gate pattern from derivedArchiveViews (Story 5 hardening) should be propagated to archiveEntries and archiveTurns needs a human ruling. The current pattern is consistent with repo convention for other tables but asymmetric with the Story 5 fix. Resolution depends on whether the Convex deployment URL is treated as a private server-to-server boundary or as a potentially leakable surface.

Whether NullPlatformStore availability outside production is acceptable for local/staging bootstrapping or should be restricted to avoid masking missing Convex config. No code change warranted without a human policy decision.

If real model/tool producers are wired before a dedicated hardening story, CANON-N002 (archive signature gap) and CANON-N005 (appendFinalizedEntry sourceObjectId strictness) are the two items most likely to surface as observable runtime bugs at that time.
